data.narrative:
Antares is a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Jordan Bramble and Julia DeWahl that has raised $470M to date. The nuclear energy sector contains 11 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or valuation-tier matches to support a reliable median comparable analysis; only one adjacent-stage peer and zero same-stage peers met filtering criteria, falling short of the three-company minimum for statistical confidence.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the applicable valuation approach. Using Antares's $470M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C-to-subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $799M. This method assumes continuation of historical funding velocity and investor confidence patterns within the nuclear energy subsector.

The triangulated range is $679M to $919M, centered on $799M. This range reflects the step-up methodology applied with conventional variance bands. Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow-peer transaction data, which limits benchmark calibration; the absence of revenue, burn rate, or technology maturity metrics; and sector-specific factors (regulatory, capital intensity, timeline to commercialization) that may not be fully captured in stage-progression heuristics. Peer comps become actionable only if portfolio companies reach sufficient scale or exit, improving data density in this early-stage subsector.
